# Raid Relic authoring rules

Codex is the sole code author. All code and documentation changes must be authored in the original thread recorded in CODEX_SESSION.md. Always resume that thread; never create or fork a thread or delegate to other agents. Work only in this repository.

Do not read auth files or credentials. No deployments, live Twitch or Devpost calls, GCP operations, IAM changes, billing linkage, or costs from Codex. Operator-verified setup for `raid-relic-hackathon`: billing linked to Firebase Payment GBP; project-specific £1 GBP monthly budget with 50/90/100 percent actual-spend alerts and default IAM email enabled; default native Standard Firestore in `us-central1`, freeTier=true, PITR disabled; run/firestore/secretmanager and billing control APIs enabled. No Cloud Run service is deployed and no client secret is present. These are facts reported as verified by the operator, not cloud state independently inspected by Codex. Do not commit until parent review.

Use Node.js 22+, node:test, Cloud Run scale-to-zero and Firestore for production. Do not substitute Cloudflare. Keep increments bounded; OAuth, encrypted tokens, bot chat and Firestore are the authorized local next increment. Mock all HTTP and cloud tests; memory is tests/dev only. Never commit secrets, local env files, or raw rollout backups.

The current Must milestone adds a backend marks engine and deterministic original SVG runes through verified chat EventSub. Marks need trusted explicit stream/session and opted-in Keeper ownership context; live lifecycle context wiring remains pending, so production startup does not enable marks by inventing a stream ID. Dedupe, per-viewer quotas and mark mutation must stay atomic. The budget is FIVE marks per viewer per stream, with a per-viewer 30-second cooldown; never cap the entire community at five. Forgetting erases own retained content/associations and receipt but preserves only existing minimal quota/cooldown identifiers until stream closure/expiry. It must not refund/extend quotas, create a channel-wide hold, or affect another viewer. Do not claim immediate erasure of all identifiers. Pending text is private; only approved rune projections may be public. Moderator commands require signed broadcaster identity or moderator badge. Keep self-forget scoped to retained application mark data; never claim Twitch-wide erasure. The next authorized increment adds the read-only OBS overlay/public snapshot/WebSocket, with no fabricated lineage or stream state. In-process fanout is single-instance only; production design is min instances 0 / max instances 1, not configured or deployed here. Local tests may bind only ephemeral loopback 5191 after canonical registry registration. Simulator state must be visibly labelled and never enabled in production. Preserve explicit reports of blocked browser/loopback tests; no screenshot/live proof may be invented. Preserve all earlier OAuth/webhook security tests.

A local 90-second ritual begins after a verified raid EventSub notification. Never claim Twitch synchronization. Future claims require participation from both incoming raiders and host chat. Run all tests after changes; do not start the application server without authorization.
7:Use Node.js 22+. Tests use Node built-ins, synthetic secrets, mock HTTP, simulated request streams, and a transactional Firestore fake. They need no credentials or cloud/Twitch network access. The four local WebSocket tests attempt the authorized fixed loopback port 5191 and clean up their ephemeral server:
19:**92 named tests: 88 pass, 4 explicitly skip, zero fail** on Node 24.22.1. All 84 earlier tests still pass. Four new socket-free tests pass; four real loopback WebSocket integration/resource tests cannot run because the sandbox denies `listen 127.0.0.1:5191` with `EPERM`. They skip only that exact permission error; port conflicts or other failures remain failures. `npm test` reports six passing files in this environment; `node --test --test-isolation=none` exposes individual results and skips. This is local verification only. The installed Firestore SDK import was verified separately without constructing a client. Actual database/emulator integration remains **UNTESTED**. Chromium launch was attempted but blocked by `sandbox_host_linux.cc:41` / `Operation not permitted`; no screenshots or successful browser/OBS validation are claimed. No login, live chat/raid, real database, or deployment validation has occurred.
21:The dependency `@google-cloud/firestore` is declared in package.json and loaded only when explicitly selecting Firestore. The parent reports successful host installation with scripts disabled and a host audit showing **0 vulnerabilities**; this audit result is operator-reported, not rerun here. This thread generated `package-lock.json` using `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --offline --no-audit --no-fund` with empty user/global npm configs, then successfully imported the actual installed SDK. No client was constructed and no credentials or database were accessed. SDK import success is not database/emulator integration validation. Tests continue to use the injected fake.
26:2. Run tests. Then, only when server startup is authorized, run `node --env-file=.env src/server.js`. Default `PORT` is **5191**. `npm start` uses exported variables; it does not load `.env` automatically.
27:3. The static Atlas is `/`, the static overlay is `/overlay`, and health is `GET /health`. Stop the preview when finished. This increment did not start a server.
54:AES-GCM uses a fresh 96-bit IV and authenticated client/role/account context. Altered ciphertext and cross-role token substitution fail decryption. `oauth.accessToken(role)` validates before every use and refreshes only after validation 401, or an explicit retry after a Helix 401. New refresh tokens are encrypted and saved only after validation. A shared-store 30-second lease serializes refresh/save operations and rejects expired writers; contention fails with a retryable busy error rather than running parallel refreshes. The default HTTP transport has an eight-second per-request timeout, rejects redirects, and redacts transport errors. Network failures after Twitch rotates a token but before storage commits can require reconnecting the account; there is no distributed transaction with Twitch.
70:**Fail-closed context:** `app.marks.setKeeperContext(hostId, { streamId, keeperId, optedIn, holdsRelic, blockedUserIds })` requires an explicit authoritative session ID, numeric Keeper ID, boolean consent/ownership, and a bounded configured blocked-user list. Acceptance requires that the Keeper ID equals the signed chat broadcaster, consent is true and the Keeper holds the relic. Only a trusted lifecycle/ownership integration may call this method. Tests inject synthetic trusted contexts; live stream lifecycle and ownership/opt-in synchronization are **not wired yet**. Runtime startup supplies no context, so real marks remain disabled. No ID is inferred from dates, raid events, names or viewer text. Updating the same active stream ID preserves viewer quotas. Selecting a new authoritative stream closes the previous session and removes its viewer quota identifiers; closed stream IDs cannot be reactivated to obtain fresh budgets. Cooldowns survive that transition until their original 30-second expiry.
72:`!mark word` or `!mark emoji` submits a mark through the already authenticated `channel.chat.message` boundary. Inputs receive Unicode NFKC, locale-independent lowercase and explicit sharp-S/final-sigma folding. The bounded conservative policy accepts one letters/combining-marks word or one supported emoji grapheme (including ZWJ families, modifiers, flags and keycaps). It rejects spaces, control/bidi/invisible word characters, HTML/link syntax and a small substring blocklist. Input is capped at 128 UTF-8 bytes and 32 normalized code points. The filter is intentionally conservative, can reject benign text, and is not comprehensive multilingual abuse/confusable moderation; moderator approval is still required.
74:`runeSvg(text)` hashes a versioned normalized value into original numeric line/diamond geometry and a fixed palette. No text interpolation, fonts, scripts, external assets or user IDs occur in SVG. Equivalent normalized input yields identical geometry. Pending marks and even their runes stay private until approval. `publicProjection(host)` returns only approved `{ id, runeSvg }` entries for the current eligible stream, with no mark text, user IDs, identity hashes/pseudonyms, timestamps or pending entries. `moderationView(host, actor)` is private and checks trusted moderator identity. No browser rendering/overlay validation is claimed.
76:**Atomic quotas:** one accepted mark per viewer per 30 seconds in the configured Keeper channel, across stream transitions; **five accepted marks per viewer per stream**, not five total community marks. The application currently supports one configured streamer. Each active session stores only `{ userId, spent }` per participant for quota enforcement, separate from mark content. Aggregate `session.spent` is diagnostic only and never a five-mark community gate. Distinct events, retries and concurrency share the same transaction for event dedupe, the viewer's cooldown/quota and mark mutation. Memory executes the same pure reducer synchronously; Firestore reads all required documents before writing in one transaction. Rejected submissions are acknowledged/deduplicated without spending viewer quota. Veto, block, opt-out and forgetting never refund viewer counters or reset active cooldowns. A genuinely new authoritative stream creates new per-viewer budgets; a closed session ID cannot be reopened.
78:Trusted services are `approve(host, actor, markId)`, `vetoLast(host, actor)`, `pause(host, actor, paused)`, `blockUser(host, actor, userId)`, `optOut(host, actor)` and self-only `forgetMe(host, actor)`. Signed chat commands are:
82:- `!relic block <numeric-user-id>` to exclude a user and remove their retained marks.
88:Configured channel blocked users and local moderation blocks are enforced before intake and approval/public projection. Channel bans are **not automatically synchronized**; the future lifecycle/ban integration must populate `blockedUserIds`. No additional OAuth scopes or live ban checks were added. The small blocklist is not a replacement for channel bans or human moderation.
92:Minimal private anti-abuse identifiers remain: the caller's existing `{ userId, spent }` quota record until that stream closes, and existing `{ userId, at }` cooldown record until 30 seconds from the accepted submission. Cooldowns are logically expired at that boundary and physically pruned on the next valid marks action; forgetting neither creates nor extends a cooldown. Repeated forgetting with no retained content adds no identity records and cannot refund quota. Selecting a new authoritative session removes the ended session's viewer counters; the old session stays closed to prevent reset-by-reopening. Forgetting does **not** erase all identifiers immediately. These retained records contain no mark text, rune, mark ID, content/history association or forget timestamp and never enter public projection. Independently configured safety block lists and OAuth/configuration data are unaffected. This is retained application mark-content erasure in the configured channel, not Twitch-wide erasure or erasure of external logs/backups.
94:**Hard storage bounds:** each channel document retains at most 16 explicit stream sessions, at most **32 participants per active stream**, at most **five marks per participant / 160 marks per stream**, and at most **160 retained mark records across all sessions**. Participant slots remain consumed for the active stream after forgetting, so content erasure cannot defeat the cap. Two block lists are capped at 128 numeric IDs each, and cross-stream cooldown entries at 128. IDs/text are length-bounded, with a **128 KiB serialized-document guard** on every mutation, well below Firestore's 1 MiB limit. At mark/participant capacity, submissions are acknowledged without mutation; session/block/document capacity errors fail closed. Retention cleanup and archival expansion are pending; a 17th retained session requires a reviewed retention policy. This per-channel ledger trades throughput for simple prototype atomicity. Event dedupe documents and public output never contain actor identities or pending mark text.
96:Tests cover normalization, unsafe inputs, original rune determinism, missing/mismatched context, cooldown boundaries, independent per-viewer five-mark limits, concurrent mixed viewers and duplicate deliveries, session reuse/reset, moderator authorization, privacy projection, pause/blocks/opt-out, content-only self-forget without global holds or quota refunds, command idempotency, bounded documents, and Firestore commit rollback/retry. Firestore tests still use the staged transactional fake; real database/emulator integration remains untested.
102:The overlay has an original faceted silver/violet crystal with a slow turn, quiet concentric **guide tracks**, and an orbit of approved original rune images. Guide tracks are not lineage growth: the UI explicitly reports **0 growth rings; lineage not implemented**. Charge is the current approved mark count out of the bounded 160-mark capacity, not inferred travel or a claim of earned lineage. Slate blue, moon silver, amber and muted violet use system serif/sans typography, no downloaded fonts/assets. Reduced-motion preference stops the turn and charge transitions. The transparent canvas and corner layout have not yet been browser/OBS visually validated due to the launch blocker.
104:`GET /api/overlay/<channel>` returns a no-store public snapshot. `ws(s)://<same-origin>/ws/<channel>` sends an initial snapshot, then genuine server-pushed snapshots after committed store events/moderation/context changes. Public fields are limited to type, process-local revision, live/simulator mode, ready/waiting/paused/unavailable status, approved rune IDs/SVG, approved count, and zero lineage rings. Neither pending text/runes, raw user IDs, private quotas/cooldowns, OAuth state nor tokens are projected. Rune SVG is generated numeric geometry and displayed as image data URLs, never inserted as raw HTML. Missing trusted stream/Keeper context yields waiting/empty state; this lifecycle is still not wired and is never invented.
106:The feed serializes in-process commits, reads and publications; connection subscription is installed before its initial read, and both server/client reject older snapshot revisions. Revisions reset on process restart and each fresh connection resets its comparator. Forget/veto/block/opt-out removal is queued to connected clients immediately after commit; actual network delivery still has latency. On connection loss/staleness the UI hides runes/charge, retries with bounded exponential backoff, and obtains a fresh initial snapshot. No database polling loop runs: reads occur on subscriptions, explicit snapshot requests and commits. Heartbeats do not read Firestore. Database failures publish unavailable/empty state without exception details.
108:Read-only WebSockets accept only the exact configured channel upgrade path, no query/subprotocol, and an exact allowed Origin. Production requires `OVERLAY_ORIGIN=https://<owned-host>` with no path/trailing slash. Local permitted origins are `http://localhost:5191` and `http://127.0.0.1:5191`; an absent/foreign Origin is rejected. Limits are 16 clients, 1 KiB incoming messages, 128 KiB outgoing snapshot and 256 KiB buffered-output cutoff; compression is disabled. Any incoming application message closes with policy violation. Every 15 seconds, ping/pong disconnects clients missing a pong on the next interval; browser heartbeat messages drive a 35-second stale watchdog. These controls are implemented, but the real-socket tests for them remain environment-blocked. Origins are a browser isolation boundary, not authentication; the projection is intentionally public and read-only.
114:The canonical workspace `config/dev-ports.json` was merged with Raid Relic on **5191**, preserving other project entries, before any listen attempt. No random fallback is used. `ws` is pinned to the installed **8.22.0**. Offline npm initially returned `ENOTCACHED` for ws metadata; the installed `node_modules/.package-lock.json` entry (resolved URL/integrity) was copied into the project lock, then `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --offline --no-audit --no-fund` completed with empty npm user/global configs. Audit is left for the parent.

117:2. For an authorized manual local test only, run `node scripts/simulate-overlay.js`, then visit `http://127.0.0.1:5191/overlay/111` and its `?corner=1` variant. The launcher binds loopback only, uses explicit synthetic stream/users/marks, and shows **Local simulator · test data**. It refuses production and is never imported by the production server. No fixture mutation endpoint exists. Stop with Ctrl-C.
118:3. Verify transparent composition, reduced motion, 160px mode, no-state, disconnect/reconnect, and approved-rune removal before claiming browser/OBS readiness. Chromium currently fails to launch in this sandbox; no screenshot artifact was created. Loopback listen also fails `EPERM`, so no working local server was left running.
129:Deadlines are persisted timestamps, with no background ritual timer. Evaluate deadlines on requests after scale-to-zero. The read-only overlay transport below is implemented; application login sessions do not exist. Validation occurs for every token use; idle hourly validation scheduling and revocation lifecycle remain pending before deployment. Cold starts/delivery latency cannot provide Twitch synchronization.
143:## Official documentation checked and remaining validation
148:- [Authorization code flow](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication/getting-tokens-oauth/): server-side exchange requires client secret and the registered redirect, and yields user access/refresh tokens.
149:- [Token validation](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication/validate-tokens/): validate tokens at startup and hourly for maintained sessions. This increment validates each use but has no persistent login sessions or idle scheduler.
156:Pending before live use: real Firestore/emulator adapter integration tests; owner correction of callback registration and final HTTPS redirect validation; actual account grants; callback reachability and webhook delivery; raid subscription permission/condition verification; retention cleanup, request rate limits and log redaction; disconnect/token-key rotation procedures; hourly idle validation if sessions are maintained; subscription reconciliation/revocation lifecycle; implementation and mock validation of committed Raid Send Off; user/claim authorization and incoming-raider proof; successful loopback WebSocket/resource tests, browser screenshots/OBS/accessibility checks; cloud security/cost review and deployment. No browser/live validation is claimed.
160:Codex authored all source, tests, documentation and the original SVG in this same thread. The initial sandbox blocker was repaired by the operator; work resumed here. The second increment added mocked OAuth, encrypted storage, bot methods and a Firestore adapter tested through injection, with its initial SDK installation failure reported honestly at the time. Parent review subsequently supplied installed dependencies; this thread generated the offline lockfile, verified the SDK import, updated committed streamer consent and reran all tests. The Must milestone then added the shared marks reducer, atomic quota/moderation integration, self-forget handling, deterministic original SVG runes and mocked regression tests. Parent review corrected the quota to five marks per viewer per stream and replaced the global forgetting hold with content erasure plus minimal bounded anti-abuse records. Curated `.codex-evidence/run-NNN.jsonl` and `.codex-evidence/SESSION_ID` are permitted; raw backups, other evidence, auth files, secrets and local env remain ignored. No raw backup or credential contents were read, no server was left running, and no commit was created. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
